title: Philosophy
text:
Effective systems start with understanding the decision being made, the constraints around it, and the risks of getting it wrong. Data is an input, not the anchor. You focus on:

The structure of the decision

The incentives and failure modes

The operational environment where the model will live

This ensures the solution is aligned with business reality, not just statistical elegance.

title: Philosophy
text:
Reduce ambiguity before increasing complexity
Ambiguity is the enemy of reliability. Before adding features, tuning models, or exploring architectures, you clarify:

What “good” looks like

What failure means

What constraints matter most

This creates a stable foundation for any technical work that follows.

title: Philosophy
text:
Design for reliability, not cleverness
High‑stakes systems must be predictable, auditable, and robust under pressure. You prioritize:

Interpretability where it matters

Hybrid approaches that blend rules and ML

Monitoring that catches drift before it becomes a problem

The goal is not novelty. The goal is trust.

title: Philosophy
text:
Align stakeholders early and often
A system is only as strong as the organization that uses it. You bring your TPM background into DS work by:

Framing ambiguity

Driving alignment across technical and non‑technical teams

Ensuring decisions are understood, not just implemented

This reduces friction and accelerates adoption.

title: Philosophy
text:
Build for the long term
Short‑term wins matter, but durability matters more. You design systems that:

Survive organizational change

Scale with new data and new constraints

Remain explainable years after deployment

This is how you create lasting impact.

title: Expertise
text:
Your modeling work centers on decisions where accuracy, interpretability, and risk management all matter. You design systems that balance statistical rigor with operational realities.

Classification and ranking systems for fraud and risk

Time‑series and forecasting for operational planning

Hybrid rule‑based and ML architectures for auditability

These systems are built to withstand scrutiny from regulators, auditors, and cross‑functional stakeholders.

title: About
text:
I’m a Principal Data Scientist specializing in high‑stakes decision systems across regulated and operationally complex domains. My work focuses on building models and workflows that organizations can trust, especially when the cost of a wrong decision is high.
I approach data science by modeling the decision, not just the dataset. That means reducing ambiguity before increasing complexity, aligning statistical rigor with operational constraints, and designing systems that are reliable, explainable, and durable in real‑world environments.
My experience spans fraud detection, clinical workflow optimization, compliance automation, and risk‑aware modeling frameworks. Across these areas, I focus on measurable impact, auditability, and the ability for systems to operate under real constraints rather than idealized assumptions.
My background blends data science, risk modeling, and technical program management. That combination helps me align stakeholders, clarify requirements, and deliver systems that work beyond the prototype stage.
